notes: Titles for Luther 1522, Scrivener 1894, Vischer 1886, Spitta 1889, Bousset 1896, Charles 1920 and Tregelles 1854 are not given in the text; bracketed descriptions stand in, from the seat names. Forenames appear only where the text gives them (Wilhelm Bousset and R. H. Charles in the SPXI packet, lines 152, 156). Eusebius's HE entry covers the witnesses read through it: Papias, Gaius, Dionysius of Alexandria, Irenaeus's date passage, Theophilus and Melito (lines 364, 394-400, 436, 522-524). Lists named as read but not quoted, all in Westcott Appendix D (line 488): Laodicea, the Apostolic Canons, the Synopsis under Chrysostom's name, Ebedjesu, the List of the Sixty, Nicephorus; folded into the Westcott entry. Hippo 393 is named via Westcott's addenda (490). Named and not cited as works read: Luther's 1545 preface (quoted by Vischer, quoting Irmischer, line 561); Tischendorf (quoted inside Rodenbiker, 490); Newton's directional test of 1733 (quoted from #1735, line 458, no title); Dieterich's crowned deities (via Charles, 414); Völter, Hilgenfeld (via Charles, 430, 561); Strauss (476); Dorotheus (561); Andreas's commentary and Arethas (402, 504); the Septuagint, Apostolic Fathers, Philo, Josephus and Greek pseudepigrapha as fields counted in #1735 (414). Declared and not pursued, so not listed: Kenyon's edition of P47 (1934), Internet Archive lending item only (599). Not listed as outside works: the epigraph attributed to Jack Feist (line 74; a heteronym of the author, set by the author per line 667); Lee Sharks's own rulings quoted in apparatus A; revelationfirst.com and its /ladder/ page (the archive's own site, 599); alexanarch.org rebuild files (LOCI.md, WITNESSES.json, PREDICTION.md); schema.org and spxi.dev in the JSON packet. The ten Google AI Overview compositions are listed one per address; they are sealed in the archive's Capture Registry and could instead be treated as archive-internal. The reviews (DeepSeek once, ChatGPT five items C, D, F, G, H) are listed as received communications; the substrate line (10) says ChatGPT reviewed four times, and F is a 'reading' rather than a review.
